pencereler.0-5: An Amtrak train derailed on a sharp curve in Philadelphia. Carriages were torn apart,
pencereler.5-12: and eight people were killed. The train entered the curve at about twice the speed limit. The engineer had
pencereler.12-20: lost track of where he was. He accelerated instead of slowing down. Automatic speed control wasn't active on that curve. Nothing stopped
pencereler.20-30: the train from overspeeding. The system was activated on the Northeast Corridor soon after.

segmentler.metin: Amtrak Train 188 derailed on a curve in Philadelphia.
It took only the train entering a curve at about twice the speed limit.
So how could the train entering a curve at about twice the speed limit do this?
The answer is overspeed on a curve, with positive train control not yet active on that section — and it is why Positive Train Control was activated on the Northeast Corridor.
